name: In Every Dream Home a Heartache
editorial_article:
"In Every Dream Home a Heartache" is a dark, cinematic centerpiece from Roxy Music’s 1973 album, *For Your Pleasure*. Written by frontman Bryan Ferry, the track stands as one of the band's most haunting experiments, blending elements of art rock and proto-punk with a chilling, detached narrative. The song is structured as a sinister monologue, where the narrator catalogs the material comforts of a high-end lifestyle only to reveal that his ultimate, obsessive companion is an inflatable plastic doll. This juxtaposition of opulence and profound alienation serves as a biting critique of consumerist hollowness.

Musically, the song is anchored by a haunting, repetitive Farfisa organ line played by Andy Mackay, which evokes a sense of gothic unease. As the song progresses, the tension builds toward an extended, feedback-laden instrumental coda led by guitarist Phil Manzanera. The track is notable for its pioneering use of studio effects; on the original vinyl release, the song appeared to fade into the run-out groove, only to return with heavily processed, phased audio. Brian Eno's contribution via the VCS 3 synthesizer and his innovative use of tape delay further cement the track's eerie, avant-garde aesthetic. Since its release, the song has maintained a cult status, cited as a foundational moment for art rock and occasionally appearing in modern cinema to underscore themes of isolation and obsession.
